description: Acceptance of the Gyrover example (single-wheel gyroscopically stabilised robot after Tsai, Ferreira and Paredis, IROS 1999). The bond graphs (RigidBody3D wheel on a RollingDisk contact, pendulum and gimbal on Revolute3D joints, Rotor3D flywheel) are compared with the equation-based reference model GyroverRef (exact rolling, Kane's equations); the steady turn is checked against the exact steady-turn solution of design/design.py, the energy book against the contact dissipation, and the controller runs against the paper's figure 3 where it can be reproduced.

checks.note: the wheel, pendulum and gimbal links follow their composed poses and the flywheel joint the displayed spin angle
the speed loop (paper K1 shifted to the set-point) reaches the 1.2 m/s cruise speed (measured 1.1997)
four 90-degree turns: the heading ends 0.025 rad short of 2 pi (measured 6.2581; the heading loop is still closing the last step)
the rounded square closes: the robot is back on its start line y = -4.42 m (measured -4.4585 m after a 33 m loop)
largest lean in the turns (measured 0.1863 rad); the lean set-point saturates at 0.35 rad and the K2 loop realises about half of it
turning rate in the middle of the second turn; the small-angle steady-turn formula of the docs at the measured lean -0.18471, speed 1.19183 m/s and tilt -0.18759 gives 0.31251 rad/s
lateral creep of the tyre stays below 0.1 mm/s (measured 4.3e-5 m/s in the turns: the friction cone is used to 3.8 %)
longitudinal creep below 0.2 mm/s (measured 7.6e-5 m/s while speeding up)
the wheel never lifts off (measured 62.0 to 79.1 N against a weight of 68.8 N)
contact penetration stays below 0.25 mm (measured 0.185 mm)
drive torque (measured peak 1.90 N m at the start)
tilt torque (measured peak 1.50 N m: it carries the gyroscopic torque in the turns)
the flywheel speed loop holds 15 000 rpm (measured 1570.72 to 1571.13 rad/s)
upper bound of the flywheel speed
energy book: stored energy + contact loss - motor work is constant to 2.8 mJ (the joint dampers of the stiff held directions dissipate the rest) while the motors do 5.5 J of work
compliant joints and an explicit contact: no derivative causality, connected and frame-consistent
the reference model drives the same loop
no damping, no drive (the tilt is held by a spring): stored energy + contact loss is constant to 3.4 mJ over 6 s
contact losses while the wheel rolls cleanly: 2.6 mJ in 2 s (vertical damping and creep)
after the nutation has grown (about 3 s) the tyre side-slips and the contact dissipates 1.18 J by 6 s
upper bound of the contact loss
the exact-rolling reference is conservative (to 0.3 mJ up to 2 s; the tilt spring energy is not in its book)
settled lean of the steady turn
settled speed
settled tilt
turning rate against the EXACT steady turn of design.steady_turn at the settled lean, speed and tilt (-0.335157 rad/s; measured -0.335169; the small-angle formula gives -0.335292)
turn radius v / psi' of the wheel centre: exact 4.4464 m (measured 4.4462 m; a circle fitted to the path gives 4.4452 m)
the tyre holds the turn with sub-millimetre-per-second creep
the reference model settles on the same steady turn
the close-up scene binds like the showcase scene
with the flywheel at 15 000 rpm the robot standing still on its rim keeps its 0.05 rad lean (measured max 0.0519 rad over 5 s: a 1.9 mrad nutation)
lower bound: the lean neither falls nor rights itself
instead it precesses slowly about the vertical (gravity moment = H x precession rate)
with the flywheel stopped the same start falls over: 0.82 rad after 0.5 s (exponential growth 6.2 1/s)
lean passes 0.5 rad at 0.427 s
the close-up scene: wheel, pendulum and gimbal follow their poses, the flywheel its displayed spin angle
paper fig. 3: the pendulum angle theta1 returns from 0.075 rad through 0 (here at 0.31 s; the paper's crosses near 0.25 s)
theta1 settled within about 1.3 s, as in the paper (where it settles within about 1 s)
pitch rate dip -0.085 rad/s at 0.17 s; the paper's figure shows about -0.08 rad/s at about 0.2 s

NOT as in the paper: the tilt does not return to 0 but settles at -0.089 rad with a 0.112 rad lean and a steady precession; the vertical angular momentum about the contact is conserved and the paper's printed K2 leaves that mode at a zero pole
the steady precession that carries the conserved vertical angular momentum
the reference model ends in the same precession
with tyre drilling damping (0.3 N m s/rad) the slow precession becomes unstable under the paper's K2: the lean grows to 0.53 rad by 8 s (dissipation destabilising a gyroscopically stabilised mode)

compare.note: bond graph vs exact-rolling reference over the 30 s mission: heading within 2.1e-5 rad
path x within 0.27 mm over 33 m (the compliant contact rolls on a 0.19 mm smaller radius)
uncontrolled rolling: heading within 7.3e-3 rad over 2 s (the free motion is sensitive; the contact compliance and the joint springs separate the runs later)
steady turn: bond graph and reference within 5.1e-6 rad/s
figure 3 scenario: pendulum angle within 3.6e-5 rad
